content: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid is either no longer recommended, only recommended as a companion agent, or not included due to insufficient data from recent analyses on extended MDR-TB regimens in adults. For example, gatifloxacin, isoniazid, and thioacetazone are not included in the guidelines for this reason. A fixed-dose combination of 500 mg amoxicillin and 125 mg clavulanic acid is administered with each dose of carbapenem, either as 125 mg twice daily or 125 mg three times daily. For further details on the use of these medications, refer to the text of the guidelines. Gatifloxacin, available as a 400 mg tablet, is not used in individuals under 18 years of age due to the lack of a quality-assured product. Similarly, thioacetazone is not used in individuals under 18 years of age for the same reason. For patients older than 14 years, a separate dosing schedule should be followed. The abbreviations used in the guidelines include: bd (twice daily), cap (capsule), dt (dispersible tablet), g (gram), im (intramuscular), iv (intravenous), kg (kilogram), ml (milliliter), mg (milligram), M/W/F (Monday, Wednesday, Friday), soln (solution), susp (suspension), and tab (tablet). The dosages were established by the Guideline Development Group for the WHO treatment guidelines for rifampicinand multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB), updated in 2018, and the WHO Global Task Force on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) of TB medicines, along with other experts. These dosages are based on the latest reviews and best practices in MDR/RR-TB treatment. For certain agents, the dosages were informed by pharmacokinetic modeling results using the principle of allometric scaling, as described by Anderson BJ and Holford NH in their work on size and maturity in pharmacokinetics. Due to the pharmacokinetic properties of certain medicines, the proposed doses may exceed the mg/kg/day ranges shown in the guidelines to achieve blood concentrations similar to target levels in an average adult patient. For patients weighing more than 30 kg, the dosing schedule for individuals older than 14 years should be followed unless otherwise indicated. If multiple dose options are provided for a specific weight band, the lower or higher option should be selected based on whether the patient is at the lower or higher limit of the body weight range. Dosing closer to the target mg/kg/day should be aimed for, which is more feasible with oral or parenteral fluids and when solid forms of different dosages are available. Fractioning tablets into halves or smaller portions should be avoided if possible. Therapeutic drug monitoring is recommended when the dose is at the upper or lower ends of the range to minimize adverse therapeutic consequences of overor under-exposure, particularly for injectable agents, linezolid, and fluoroquinolones. Clinicians may decide to exceed the recommended values in specific cases to improve therapeutic outcomes. Dissolving tablets in 10 ml of water may facilitate administration in patients in lower weight bands and avoid fractioning solid formulations, although bioavailability may be uncertain. The use of dispersible tablets is preferred if available. For individuals weighing more than 44 kg, a dose of 600 mg once daily is proposed. In children aged 3–5 years, half of a 50 mg adult tablet may be used, but this does not result in the same blood levels observed in trials using the special 25 mg pediatric tablet. Bioavailability may be further altered when the 50 mg tablet is split, crushed, or dissolved. Weight-based daily dosing is intended for administration 6 or 7 days per week, although M/W/F scheduling may allow for higher dosing. Streptomycin may be diluted in three different ways, and dosing closer to the upper limit of the mg/kg/day range is more desirable. For intravenous use, the volume may be increased. In the 2018 WHO treatment guidelines, certain agents are no longer recommended (e.g., kanamycin, capreomycin), only recommended as companion agents (e.g., amoxicillin/clavulanic acid), or not included due to insufficient data from recent analyses on extended MDR-TB regimens in adults (e.g., gatifloxacin, isoniazid, thioacetazone). Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid is only available in combination with amoxicillin as co-amoxiclav. For the 24–30 kg weight band, a dose of 125 mg twice daily or 125 mg three times daily is recommended. For further details on the use of these medications, refer to the text of the guidelines.
